subject: Dedicated pool hotspot — mitigation runbook & exec visibility request
messages:
From: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@finflow.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency + 429s on Dedicated pool (FinFlow production)

Naomi —

We started seeing a spike in median latency and a steady rise in 429/queueing errors around 08:40 PDT this morning on our dedicated pool. Traffic is within our agreed reserved capacity (we're not bursting beyond committed tokens). Quick metrics from our side:
- median token latency up from ~35ms to ~220ms over last 20m
- 429 errors increased from ~0.1% to ~4.6%
- request queue depth showing sustained >250 waiting requests for ~15 minutes

This is impacting synchronous inference paths for payment validation and causing customer-facing failures. We tried failing over to your hosted fallback but our integration has tight latency requirements and the routing switch isn't fully transparent for long-polling flows.

We need immediate assistance — can you confirm whether the dedicated pool is saturated or if there's a scheduling regression on your end? We're happy to provide logs but would prefer Redwood drive steps for mitigation we can coordinate on.

Sam 
Samuel Cho
Engineering Lead, Platform
FinFlow
ops@finflow.com

P.S. Attached: sample trace IDs (inlined below)
Trace: ff2a-21b6, ff2a-21b7, ff2a-21c0
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@finflow.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency + 429s on Dedicated pool (FinFlow production)

Sam — thank you, and I'm really sorry you're seeing this. I'm opening an incident now and looping in infra/ops and our leadership so we can move quickly. Initial next steps from our side: 

1) Immediate: enable tenant-level throttles for non-critical backfills and evict any queued maintenance jobs. This should clear headroom within 5-10 minutes.
2) Fallback: we'll enable an expedited routing override to send critical inference paths to a warmed hosted pool with priority routing (expect ~60-100ms extra latency but avoids 429s).
3) Collect: please upload the traces/logs to the Drive link (or send attachments) — Jonas will pull the kernel-level metrics.

I'm attaching a short mitigation runbook (runbook_mitigation_v1.pdf) with the steps above and expected signal checks. Jonas — can you validate whether this looks like a scheduling/cgroup contention vs. a kernel regression? Marissa — can you prepare an executive note if we need to request short-term SLA leniency/credits? Irene — flagging for your visibility; if headroom cannot be recovered in 30m we should consider an exec bridge.

I'll update every 10 minutes and confirm when the routing override is active.

—Naomi
Naomi Feldman
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Samuel Cho <samuel.cho@finflow.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 09:36:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Severe latency + 429s on Dedicated pool (FinFlow production)

Naomi / Sam — quick technical snapshot after initial heap/profile capture (attaching finflow_logs_20270621.zip):
- Observed hot-threads tied to the serving scheduler: several inference worker processes are holding large KV cache locks while lower-priority maintenance tasks are queued and consuming fractional GPU slots.
- Scheduler appears to have degraded fairness for long-seq requests, resulting in head-of-line blocking and queue pileups.
- No immediate CUDA driver errors; GPU utilization is high (~92%) but there is a mismatch between active contexts and reserved token throughput.

Immediate actions I've pushed: 
- Evicted queued maintenance jobs for FinFlow tenant and disabled background transfers for the pool (should free ~12-16% headroom).
- Applied tenant-level soft caps for non-critical task classes.
- Will flip on the routing override Naomi proposed in 2m and monitor 1/5/15m latency windows.

If metrics do not recover within 15-20m we'll escalate to capacity expansion (provision a temporary additional shard) — that requires Ops approval and a short lead time to spin up.

I'll keep collecting kernel metrics and GPU-side traces; attaching the logs here.

- Per the logs and Jonas' snapshot, this looks like a scheduling-imbalance leading to fairness regressions in the serving scheduler. We need an RCA but treat the incident as a capacity/scheduling bug until proven otherwise.
- Naomi: prepare a concise one-paragraph status for the customer (Marissa will send). Provide a short timeline for the permanent fix and a proposed date for a postmortem (tentatively Wed 2027-06-30).
- Ops: provision a temporary shard for FinFlow if headroom recovers less than 10% after the evictions; target spin-up within 2 hours and confirm cost implications. Marissa: hold pause on any credit commitments until we have the postmortem scope.
- Please upload all captured traces and the preliminary mitigation runbook to the linked Drive folder and create the JIRA ticket for the engineering fix path (JIRA-REDWOOD-1287).

I'll join the postmortem and will escalate to the resume leadership call only if we need longer-term architecture changes that affect other customers. Good work moving fast — let's keep communication tight.
